record.paper_title: Open Questions about Time and Self-reference in Living Systems
record.original_question: How useful is coalgebra for describing self-referential systems while they undergo structural evolution, given that coalgebra offers clarity for self-reference but may not handle evolving system structure adequately?

evidence.quote:
Coalgebra offers one promising approach to
dealing with systems characterised by self-reference. It has the advantage of providing the same clarity
and certainty offered by earlier mathematics. However, it is not clear how useful it will be in describing
systems as they undergo structural evolution.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Recall that a coalgebra for an endofunctor $F:\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{C}$ on a category $\mathcal{C}$ is a pair $(X,\gamma)$ consisting of an object $X\in\mathcal{C}$ together with a morphism $\gamma:X\to F(X)$, and that final $F$-coalgebras provide canonical models of self-referential and infinitely-unfolding behaviour (e.g.\ streams, transition systems, non-well-founded sets). A morphism of $F$-coalgebras $(X,\gamma)\to(Y,\delta)$ is a morphism $f:X\to Y$ with $F(f)\circ\gamma=\delta\circ f$.

Coalgebra in this fixed-functor sense describes the dynamics of a system whose "type of observations/transitions" $F$ is held constant. By a structurally evolving system we informally mean a system whose very state-space type changes over time, i.e.\ a family $\{F_t\}_{t\in T}$ of endofunctors indexed by a (possibly continuous or branching) parameter $t$, together with coalgebras $\gamma_t:X_t\to F_t(X_t)$ and coherent comparison data between different indices $t,t'\in T$.

Problem. Develop a mathematically precise framework — for instance based on indexed/fibred categories of coalgebras, lax or oplax natural transformations between the functors $F_t$, or bialgebraic/distributive-law techniques — that simultaneously
(i) retains the universal-property characterisation of self-reference enjoyed by final coalgebras for a single endofunctor, and
(ii) coherently models structural evolution, in which the endofunctor $F_t$ itself, and hence the carrier $X_t$, may change with $t$.
Then determine: to what extent can such a framework faithfully describe self-referential systems undergoing structural evolution? Specifically, identify necessary and sufficient conditions on the family $\{F_t\}$ and on the transition data under which a "final evolving coalgebra" exists and uniquely captures self-referential behaviour across structural change, or, conversely, prove obstructions showing that no such generalisation can preserve both clarity of self-reference and adequacy for structural evolution.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open conceptual problem about the adequacy of coalgebraic methods for systems undergoing structural evolution. No published resolution of this specific question was identified; related work on indexed/parametrised coalgebras and bialgebraic semantics exists but does not settle the issue.

status_evidence.title: Open Questions about Time and Self-reference in Living Systems (abstract)
status_evidence.snippet: The work explicitly raises coalgebra's adequacy for structural evolution as an open question.
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed as open.
